title: Second-Order Policy Effects as State Transitions: A Source-Linked Benchmark for Policy Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2608.15101v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Policy evaluation often estimates direct benefits and costs while treating the institutional environment as fixed. In practice, a policy changes the system it enters: actors adapt, enforcement capacity shifts, burdens move, and new equilibria form around capture, gaming, compliance theater, irreversibility, and repair costs. We formalize this as second-order policy-effect prediction and present a source-linked benchmark for policy simulation. The benchmark contains 96 named public-policy cases across eight domains and four balanced action classes: implement, modify, pilot, and block. Each case includes source locators and state variables for benefit, capture, gaming, burden shift, instability, uncertainty, irreversibility, distributional risk, and implementation capacity. translated_title: 二阶政策效应作为状态转换：一个用于政策模拟的源链接基准
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.15101v1 公告类型：新 摘要：政策评估通常估计直接收益和成本，同时将制度环境视为固定不变。在实践中，一项政策会改变其所进入的系统：行为者适应、执行能力转变、负担转移，并在捕获、博弈、合规表演、不可逆性和修复成本周围形成新的均衡。我们将此形式化为二阶政策效应预测，并提出了一个用于政策模拟的源链接基准。该基准包含96个命名的公共政策案例，涵盖八个领域和四个平衡的动作类别：实施、修改、试点和阻止。每个案例包括源定位器和关于收益、捕获、博弈、负担转移、不稳定性、不确定性、不可逆性、分配风险和实现能力的状态变量。运行器从案例表中重新生成方法输出和聚合结果，模拟器从不读取专家动作目标。我们报告了基于协议的翻译结果。
tldr: 本文提出了一个包含96个公共政策案例的源链接基准，用于预测政策进入系统后的二阶效应（如捕获、博弈和不可逆性），并支持政策模拟中的实施、修改、试点或阻止决策。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a source-linked benchmark with 96 public-policy cases to predict second-order policy effects (e.g., capture, gaming, irreversibility) and support policy simulation decisions of implementation, modification, piloting, or blocking.
